QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_2

question.text: Ms. Ananya Krishnan, Chief Investment Officer at Saraswati Capital, is structuring a new fund that will invest primarily in late-stage unlisted growth companies through equity and equity-linked instruments with no leverage at fund level. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, this fund MUST be registered as:

answer.text: Category I AIF — Venture Capital Fund sub-category
Category III AIF — because unlisted growth equity employs complex strategies
Category II AIF — Private Equity Fund
Specified AIF — because private equity is not a defined sub-category

explanation.text: The Logic: Private Equity Funds invest primarily in equity/equity-linked instruments or partnership interests of investee companies and, having no specific incentives/concessions from the government, fall under Category II AIF which does not undertake leverage/borrowing beyond permitted limits. VCFs (Cat I) target start-ups/early-stage, not late-stage. The Trap: Option A confuses later-stage PE with early-stage VC. Option C wrongly assumes any equity strategy equals Cat III; Cat III is defined by complex/leveraged trading strategies, not unlisted growth equity. Option D misuses the Specified AIF classification (a separate fourth category inserted by SEBI in 2023, not a catch-all). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests Cat I/II at Distributor level; XIX-C expects the Manager to articulate WHY a PE fund falls into Cat II (no specific incentives + no fund-level leverage) rather than Cat I. Manager's Pro-Tip: When drafting the PPM category election, remember that registration in Cat II is default for any AIF that neither qualifies for a Cat I incentive (start-up, SME, infra, social, angel, SSF) nor employs Cat III's complex strategies — don't chase Cat I framing unless the investee universe truly qualifies.
